title: Two model-screened magnesium alloy routes passed tensile tests
summary: A model-screened magnesium alloy containing gadolinium and yttrium reached 296 MPa yield strength and 398 MPa tensile strength in lab tests. A separate route using recycled feedstock produced AZ31 with similar mechanical properties to its primary-feedstock comparison. The study estimated 40.4% lower operating costs and 88.9% lower emissions for that route.
ai_technology: Physics-informed ensemble of random forests and XGBoost
organization: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Max Planck Institute for Sustainable Materials

source_review.scope: Primary v1 PDF front matter, ensemble training, Methods, and experimental validation in Figures 3–4

evidence.tested: The study screened composition and microstructure candidates, selected two routes and tested prepared materials with tensile measurements and microstructural characterization.
evidence.unknown: The cost and emissions figures are modeled for the study’s feedstock and process assumptions. The two lab-scale cases do not establish production-scale performance or savings.
evidence.ai_role: The fitted ensemble predicted strength and linked candidate microstructures to processing routes, supporting selection of the two experimentally tested alloys.
